# I Ching · The Book of Changes

> A quiet, minimalist online I Ching (Yijing) oracle. Visitors form a question,
> cast a hexagram by yarrow-stalk probabilities or the three-coin method, and
> read its Judgment, Image, and Counsel. Free to use; no account required.
> Optional free accounts let users keep a personal reading journal.

This site is a reference-plus-tool around the I Ching. The content is
deliberately plain-language and factually conservative so it can be safely
quoted by answer engines.

## Key facts

- The I Ching (also romanised Yijing) is an ancient Chinese text meaning
  "Book of Changes". Its core dates to the Western Zhou period, c. 1000–750 BCE.
- It consists of 64 hexagrams — six-line figures of broken (yin) and unbroken
  (yang) lines. Each hexagram has a traditional name, number, Judgment, and
  Image.
- Any hexagram decomposes into two stacked trigrams (three-line figures).
  There are 8 trigrams: Heaven, Earth, Thunder, Water, Mountain, Wind, Fire,
  Lake. 8 × 8 = 64.
- A reading is cast by generating six lines, from the bottom up, by chance.
  Standard methods are the yarrow-stalk procedure and the three-coin method.
- In the three-coin method, heads = 3 (yang) and tails = 2 (yin). Three coins
  sum to 6 (old yin, changing), 7 (young yang), 8 (young yin), or 9 (old yang,
  changing).
- A changing line flips polarity to generate a second "relating" hexagram,
  indicating where the situation is moving.
- The I Ching is a text, not a religion. It is used in Confucian, Daoist, and
  secular philosophical traditions.

## Primary pages

- [Consult the oracle (home)](/): The interactive oracle. Form a question,
  pick a casting method, and cast a hexagram.
- [About the I Ching](/about): Plain-language reference: what the I Ching is,
  how the 64 hexagrams are constructed, how to cast a reading, how to read
  Judgment, Image, and changing lines. Includes a glossary.

## Structured data

Each page emits schema.org JSON-LD: `WebSite` and `WebApplication` on the
root, `Article` and `FAQPage` on `/about`, `FAQPage` on `/`, and per-reading
`Article` blocks when a reading is opened by its owner.

## What this site is not

- Not a fortune-telling service. The I Ching is presented as a reflective
  tool, not a predictor.
- Not affiliated with any religious organisation.
- Not a commercial marketplace. Readings and journaling are free.

## Contact

This is an independent personal project.
